title: Fed decision in April?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Polymarket traders price a 99.1% implied probability of no change to the Federal Reserve's 3.50%-3.75% federal funds target range at the April 28-29, 2026 FOMC meeting, reflecting strong consensus amid recent data. March 2026 CPI surged 0.9% monthly to 3.3% year-over-year—highest since mid-2024—driven by a 10.9% gasoline spike from geopolitical oil shocks, while nonfarm payrolls added 178,000 jobs and unemployment dipped to 4.3%. The Fed held steady in March, with minutes showing officials open to hikes if inflation persists but eyeing one later-2026 cut. This data-dependent stance leaves scant room for near-term moves, though surprise weakness in April 17 jobs data or pre-meeting inflation prints could marginally challenge the hold.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom commands trader consensus at 28% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, driven by his term-limited California governorship ending in 2026, recent dominance in a March POLITICO California primary poll over Kamala Harris, and sustained national visibility through anti-Trump critiques and a March book tour discussing potential matchups. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez trails at 8.3% on strong progressive grassroots energy amid speculation of a presidential or Senate bid, while Harris sits at 6.6% following her April 10 statement considering another White House run despite 2024 baggage. Jon Ossoff's 5.9% reflects rising buzz from Georgia's battleground wins. This wide-open field, with no declared candidates, could consolidate around 2026 midterm performers in swing states, early fundraising leaders, and DNC endorsements, as governors like Newsom and Shapiro differentiate via executive records versus senators' legislative profiles.

Kennedy Jr. at 49% implied probability to secure the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, ahead of Vice President J.D. Vance (38.5%) and Secretary of State Marco Rubio (21.6%), diverging from recent straw polls like CPAC where Vance led with 53% and Rubio at 35%. Vance benefits from incumbency and top rankings in New Hampshire and youth polls, while Rubio gains from donor draft efforts and elevated visibility in foreign policy amid Iran tensions, with primaries slated for early 2027.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Negotiators from the United States and Iran have pivoted to an interim nuclear suspension deal following the collapse of comprehensive peace talks in Islamabad on April 11 after 21 hours of direct discussions mediated by Pakistan. Persistent rifts remain over Iran's uranium enrichment rights and U.S. demands for permanent curbs, missile limits, and sanctions relief, amid a fragile ceasefire enforced by American naval blockades of Iranian ports and the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump expressed optimism for a breakthrough, citing military leverage from prior strikes, while Vice President Vance highlighted Iran's refusal of zero-enrichment terms. Upcoming resumption in Pakistan and a potential two-week truce extension could catalyze progress toward a durable agreement, though Gulf and European officials forecast months of diplomacy ahead.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes' commanding early-season pace under 2026 regulations has locked George Russell and rookie Kimi Antonelli as the clear frontrunners in trader consensus for the Drivers' Championship, with Russell's 43.5% implied probability edging Antonelli's 30.4% on his proven experience despite the Italian leading standings 72-63 after four Grands Prix. Russell's Australian GP win initiated Mercedes' 1-2 dominance, but Antonelli's flawless back-to-back victories in China and Japan—his latest at Suzuka on March 29—propelled him atop the leaderboard, narrowing the intra-team battle to nine points. Rivals like Verstappen languish amid Red Bull's adaptation struggles, emphasizing Mercedes' superior energy management and qualifying edge as key sentiment drivers.
